answer: Latency-Weighted Queue Priority: each identity earns scheduling priority proportional to its rolling 30-day consistency of completed work, decaying like an ember without fresh output. New identities start at zero priority and wait behind established ones, so flooding the queue with fresh accounts adds delay rather than capacity. An attacker must run every fake identity through real task cycles for weeks to thaw priority, paying compute and time per account; parallel sybils split that cost across a tundra of idle slots. A dormant account loses plume of reputation fast, forcing continuous spend.
